root_cause: The run produced only the simulation watchdog timeout, with no trace mismatches and no compile errors, so this is a liveness failure rather than a wrong-data result. The core either never reaches the ECALL/halt commit point or a structural stall/handshake never completes. The first candidate is a dead or undriven control wire at top-level integration (halted/exit_code, stop-fetch/ecall_pending, or a completion/ready signal), followed by permanent backpressure in issue/rename/ROB or a load-store/cache response path. The brief has no PC-freeze pattern, so the exact stage cannot be isolated from the text alone.
repair_constraints: Keep every module, file, and port name/width exactly as in the plan/interface contract; do not rename or delete ports or modules.
Preserve synchronous active-low reset behavior at the rising clk edge, including dmem_valid=0 during reset and PC priority reset > redirect > ECALL halt freeze > load-use stall > PC+4.

Preserve halt/retire timing: ECALL must survive ID-to-WB, each committed instruction produces exactly one single-cycle dbg_retire_valid, halted and exit_code appear together on the next edge after ECALL commit, and all outputs/architectural state remain stable after halt.

Preserve external handshakes: at most one outstanding request per interface, hold valid/addr until ready, never abort an in-flight request on flush/halt, suppress only the response via epoch, and keep imem_addr[1:0]=00 while running.
Keep the load-use stall at exactly one cycle, preserve EX/MEM-over-MEM/WB forwarding and same-address WB-to-ID read behavior, and do not add stalls/flushes outside load-use or redirect.
Cache refill requests must remain asserted until handshaken, stores must not merge stale lines, and external request valid must not be gated by halted/flush.
